subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Lidar and Proximity Sensors
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lidar and Proximity Sensors.

hook.text: A mobile robot fires laser pulses and measures how long they take to bounce back. It maps the room in milliseconds.

buildup.text: Lidar creates a 3D point cloud of the surroundings. The robot sees walls, obstacles, and people as clusters of dots.

discovery.text: SLAM algorithms combine lidar data with motion estimates to build a map while navigating — no prior map needed.

twist.text: Lidar struggles with glass and mirrors. The laser passes through or bounces unpredictably. Other sensors fill the gap.

climax.text: Self-driving cars, delivery robots, and warehouse AGVs all depend on lidar for real-time spatial awareness.

punchline.text: Shoot light. Measure time. Know the world around you.

quiz.question: What does SLAM allow a mobile robot to do?
options: Control its speed based on the surface friction detected by the wheels
Simultaneously build a map and determine its position within that map
Communicate with other robots to avoid collisions in shared spaces
